newsitem.title: USA: Former congressman Reynolds on hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Former congressman Reynolds on hunger strike.

text.p: Former congressman Mel Reynolds, serving a five-year jail term for sexual misconduct, may be force fed if he refuses to end a hunger strike he began 11 days ago, a judge has ruled.

Reynolds told a federal judge Wednesday that he stopped eating to protest jail conditions and a lack of access to his lawyer. He is being held at a high-rise jail in downtown Chicago where he was transferred to await trial on bank fraud charges.
Judge Charles Norgle of the U.S. District Court gave jail officials permission Wednesday to begin feeding Reynolds through a tube inserted in his nose if he refuses to abandon his fast.
Jail officials said Thursday they did not yet know if Reynolds had decided to start eating again.
Reynolds, a Democrat, resigned his House seat after he was convicted of having sex with an underage campaign worker.
